title: Runtime verification binds against a local Keycloak container; cloud-tenant smokes are accountBound
description: Runtime-verify ACs on this blueprint bind against a local Keycloak realm the project stands up per REQ-009 (or an equivalent locally-runnable realm the project already operates). The local realm is real Keycloak on the wire: discovery, JWKS, `token_endpoint`, `introspection_endpoint`, and `end_session_endpoint` all speak the standards-tracked shapes the verifier and the flow controller consume. ACs that require a smoke test against a project-owned cloud-hosted Keycloak deployment or a managed Keycloak service are `accountBound`: the runtime-verify runner marks them with an `accountBound` flag and a stable-coded skip reason (`KEYCLOAK_LIVE_REALM_UNREACHABLE`) when the project does not have live deployment credentials in the runtime environment; the CI pipeline does not fail on a skipped accountBound AC, and the ship gate reads the honest coverage. A project that has live credentials wires them and the accountBound smokes light up. The introspection-mode AC (US-11105) similarly binds against a local stub introspection responder shipped as a shape in `assets/mock-introspection/`; a project may substitute a second local Keycloak realm configured for opaque tokens or an equivalent implementation.
rationale: Keycloak is self-hostable; the local-container path is the honest runtime-verify surface and needs no external account. Cloud-hosted realm smokes are still valuable for a project that operates one but are not achievable in every CI environment, so the accountBound posture keeps CI honest without demanding a cloud realm every consumer maintains. The introspection stub covers the shape of the alternate verification mode without demanding a second Keycloak container per test suite (though a project may run one if it prefers a real endpoint).
